correctness.rationale: The exact product gives \(\Pr(L\ge k)=k^{-\beta_n}\) and \(\Pr(H>k)=(k+2)^{-\beta_n}\). The log-Riemann sum gives \(\mathbb E(L\wedge n)\sim a(c)\log n\); second truncated moments \(O_c(n)\), plus union bound on L>n, give uniform renewal-clock concentration at \(n/\log n\) scale. Mark-tail measure \(b_n\Pr(H/b_n>z)\to e^{-c}/z\) and Laplace products imply iid Poisson marks. Uniform clock replacement, random-index bracketing and a small-band bound establish physical-time Poisson convergence and exclude the unfinished excursion from the max limit. Strict derivative of lambda gives monotonicity; 328 reproducible finite numerical/exact assertions complement, not replace, these proofs.

value.rationale: The first-order maximum and complete excursion space-time law are a natural observable of a birth-catastrophe population model and quantify rare high peaks on the physical observation clock. The crossover \(\beta_n=1+c/\log n\) is the critical scale where finite-horizon growth straddles positive/null recurrence, and yields a nonconstant explicit intensity \(c/(e^c-1)\). A marked-process limit and treatment of the unfinished excursion are more informative than fixed-exponent stationary tails or a routine finite-parameter substitution.
